The Qur'anic context here addresses those who fall into this forbidden statement and this sinful comparison, saying to them: beware of this saying, and distinguish between the mother and the wife. The mother is the one who gave birth; the wife is never a mother, and it is not fitting that we call her "mother."

So put matters in their proper place: the mother is a mother, and the wife is a wife, and each of them has its own limits.

Then he makes clear to them that this statement ("You are to me like the back of my mother") is a reprehensible utterance: ﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾. The munkar (objectionable, that which sound reason and healthy taste reject) is the saying that reason denies and sound taste rejects, and the zur (falsehood) is lying and vanity. Among the objectionable and the false is that you liken a wife to a mother, or a mother to a wife. He, glory be to Him, wishes to annul this saying from the tongues of the Muslims, just as He annulled the practice of adoption in the story of Sayyidna Zayd ibn Harithah, which you know.

The verse concludes with His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, meaning: for what has passed from you and what has preceded of your transgressions.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 58, verse 21:

Victory belongs to Allah, the Exalted, along with His success and His power. They are His servants and His messengers to His creation, so how would He abandon them or leave them?...

So then: the triumph of truth over falsehood is one of the sunan (divine laws, sing. sunnah) of Allah in His universe. Why, then, do we now see falsehood triumphing over truth? We say: if you see the people of faith being defeated before the people of disbelief, know that the cause lies within them, because they have violated the conditions of soldiership (al-jundiyyah) that guarantee them victory...

Allah, glorified and exalted, wishes to establish this reality and to firmly fix it in the souls of the believers, so that they may grow more confident in Allah's support for them. His words, exalted is He, ﴿لأغلبن﴾ ("I will surely overcome"): the lam is for oath and emphasis, as if He, glorified is He, swears and says: "By My might and My majesty, I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Then the emphatic nun in ﴿لأغلبن﴾...

﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾. This is the reason for the victory: He, glorified is He, is the Strong who overcomes by the essence of His strength, and He, glorified is He, is the (Mighty), meaning the One who cannot be overcome. Had He willed, He would have triumphed over them and seized them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. But He wills that you, O believers, have the honor of victory over them: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ [At-Tawbah 9:14].
